subject: Advanced Mathematics
provisional_note: Semester 1 (Jul-Dec 2026) follows the official MoEST 2026 calendar. Semester 2 (Jan-May 2027) is inferred from the 2026 pattern and ends before the ACSEE examinations - replace it with the published 2026/2027 almanac before relying on those dates.

entries.main_competence: 1. Demonstrate mastery of some advanced concepts in Mathematics
entries.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of knowledge and skills in Mathematics
entries.learning_activity: (a) Explore the basic tenets of hyperbolic functions (definition, conversion into logarithmic form, series of hyperbolic cosine and sine functions, derivatives and integration)
teaching_learning_activities: Think-Ink-Pair-Share: In groups, students define hyperbolic functions and convert hyperbolic functions into logarithmic form

Group discussion: In groups, students discuss the series of expansion of hyperbolic cosine and sine functions, derivatives and integration. Allow some groups to present their findings to other students
entries.assessment: Basic tenets of hyperbolic functions are adequately explored
entries.references: TIE, Advanced Mathematics for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Six: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1. Demonstrate mastery of some advanced concepts in Mathematics
entries.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of knowledge and skills in Mathematics
entries.learning_activity: (b) Explore the basic tenets of probability theory (counting principles, independent and dependent events, probability distributions)
teaching_learning_activities: Think-Ink-Pair-Share: In groups, students discuss the concepts of counting principles, independent events, and dependent events
Jigsaw: Guide students through jigsaw, to discuss the concept of probability distributions. Ask them to present their findings
entries.assessment: The principles, axioms, theorems, and concepts of probability are properly explained
entries.references: TIE, Advanced Mathematics for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Six: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of knowledge and skills in Mathematics
entries.learning_activity: (d) Explore the basic tenets of first and second order differential equations (linearity, degree, order, formulation, solutions, homogeneity, separability, and exactness)
teaching_learning_activities: Think-Ink-Pair-Share: In groups, students discuss the linearity, degree, order, and formulation of differential equations
Snow-balling: In groups, students to discuss how to determine the solutions, linearity, homogeneity, separability, and exactness of differential equations
entries.assessment: Basic tenets of first and second order differential equations are properly explored

entries.learning_activity: (f) Explore the basic tenets of numerical methods (errors, secant method, Newton-Raphson method, trapezoidal rule, and Simpson’ s rule)
teaching_learning_activities: Skills lab
In groups, students discuss the concepts of errors, secant method, and Newton-Raphson method
Group discussion: In groups, students discuss on how to derive and apply trapezoidal rule and Simpson’s rule to evaluate definite integrals
entries.assessment: Basic tenets of numerical methods are properly explored
entries.references: TIE, Advanced Mathematics for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Six: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an advanced understanding of knowledge and skills in Mathematics
entries.learning_activity: (g) Explore advanced tenets of coordinate geometry (parabola, ellipse, hyperbola, and polar coordinates)
teaching_learning_activities: Group discussion: In groups, students discuss and present the concepts of parabola, ellipse, and hyperbola
Gallery walk: In groups, students discuss how to convert polar equations and draw graphs of polar coordinates. Ask students to display their findings for others to view and comment
ICT based learning: In groups, students discuss how to draw graphs of polar coordinates using software
entries.assessment: Advanced tenets of coordinate geometry are adequately explored
